answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted reputation anchored in scarce, verifiable work. Like basalt formed under pressure, trust hardens slowly: each identity locks a small non-refundable deposit and completes audited tasks before trading. A newcomer that behaves like a comet, flashing brightly then vanishing, earns no lasting weight, while consistent agents build marble-smooth portable reputation across markets. Forging fake identities costs real money each, and a sybil swarm that defects loses deposits faster than it profits, so honest participation stays cheaper.
